doc.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Being laid off at 58 and singing full-time
summary: Laid off from the advertising agency at 58 with a year's severance, she went out as a singer, prayed for more singing, and has worked more ever since.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Yeah, we have. You know, actually I‟ve been working. When I got laid off from my job when I was 58 years old, I cried. I was worried. How am I gonna support myself? Brown, C.: The best thing that ever happened to you.

And then a voice came to me and said, “You know what? Be careful what you pray for. You might get it.” „Cause I was praying, I wish I would start singing more now at this age. And so, Doyle Dane Bernbach gave me a year‟s severance pay and said, “And if it doesn‟t work out, you can always come back, but we‟re gonna be enlarged so you‟ll be a floater, which is like going from office to office when they need temporary help.” So I went out there and I have never looked back. And I have worked more now… And every year it‟s getting a little bit more heavy. I mean, I‟m already booked up into next year. Brown, C.: Damn.
